title: extern, static, and header files

spans.text: In a header, `extern` declares a global variable without defining storage; define it once in a `.cpp` file. A function-local `static` keeps its value between calls, while file-scope `static` limits a name to that file. `#pragma once` prevents a header from being included repeatedly; `#ifndef`/`#define`/`#endif` is the portable guard pattern. Arduino IDE may combine `.ino` files, so use explicit headers and `.cpp` files as projects grow.

spans.title: Important note
spans.text: Do not put a non-inline variable definition in a shared header; multiple definitions can fail at link time. `#pragma once` is widely supported but is not a standard C++ directive. Avoid circular includes by keeping headers dependent on declarations where possible.
